headline: Easy-run HR holds well below the prior block into the recovery week, strengthening the case for a real efficiency gain.
confidence_reasons: Multiple data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
The lower easy-run HR you saw building through the recent block has carried into a lighter week rather than snapping back — which is exactly the signal that separates a genuine aerobic efficiency gain from a recovery-week artefact. It's holding at comparable effort across a decent number of runs, so this is looking more like a durable adaptation than noise. Worth noting it's not confirmed until volume steps back up, but the direction is encouraging.

The recent block landed a meaningful step up in volume over the prior four weeks while doubling strength frequency, and you've absorbed it without the strain ratio drifting out of productive territory. That combination — more running, more lifting, HR trending down — is the picture of a base that's consolidating rather than being overreached. Zone distribution stays heavily aerobic with very little grey-zone drift, which is what you want with the event roughly four weeks out and a self-supported, pack-carrying effort ahead.

Nothing in today's data argues for changing course. The recovery week is doing its job.
watch_items: Whether the lower easy-run HR survives the return to higher volume — the confirming test for this efficiency gain.
Whether pack-carry running enters the schedule while there's still time to adapt the carry demand before the coast-to-coast.
Whether ascent per run starts building toward sustained climbing rather than the rolling profiles logged so far, given the mountain crossing.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 190 km vs 126 km prior block (+51%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 145 bpm vs 153 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 9 vs 8 runs)
▲ Zone 2: 444 min vs 180-240 min/week target (246% of minimum); grey zone (Z3+Z4): 5.2%
▬ Strain:tolerance ratio 1.09 (PRODUCTIVE) (strain 94, tolerance 87); sleep averaging 7h36m over the same period
